news.title: Senator Imasuen hails Flamingos after World Cup win
news.lede: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Ethics, Privileges and Public Petitions, Senator Neda Imasuen, has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos on their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, describing it as a landmark achievement for Nigeria and African football. Imasuen, who represents Edo South Senatorial District, praised the players for their resilience, determination and fighting spirit, which propelled them to become the first African nation to win the competition. In a congratulatory statement issued through his media aide, Moshood Karim, and made available to journalists in Abuja, the senator said the team’s journey from an opening-day defeat to six consecutive victories before lifting the trophy demonstrated their character, discipline and belief. The Flamingos made history on Saturday in Morocco after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final to claim the 2026 title.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.

news.title: Nigeria make history: Morocco send a strong message ahead of the 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Morocco continued testing its organisational capabilities and sporting and logistical infrastructure by hosting the Women's Under-17 World Cup. The tournament concluded in the capital Rabat with Nigeria crowned champions for the first time in their history, after a 2-1 victory over Japan. It marked a new stage in the kingdom's preparations to host the 2030 World Cup in partnership with Spain and Portugal. Spanish newspaper "Sport" reported that the tournament's importance went beyond the sporting competition, offering Morocco an additional opportunity to test its facilities, organisational mechanisms, delegation management and logistical operations as part of the plan to prepare for football's showpiece in 2030.

news.title: 'No withdrawals' as Poland prepares to host FIFA tournament amid Infantino backlash
news.lede: It will be the first FIFA competition since UEFA voted to support a boycott of FIFA events. Hosts Poland said on Tuesday that preparations for next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup remain on schedule, as the tournament prepares to become the first FIFA event staged amid the backlash against global football chief Gianni Infantino. It will be the first FIFA competition since UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously voted to support a boycott of FIFA events after Infantino proposed and then abandoned a plan to carve off the commercial rights to the World Cup and sell 20% of them to private investors to raise about $4.2 billion. That triggered a massive football governance dispute.
